mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to lower corporate margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for three consecutive months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS above their respective 5-year averages within the same month signals a simultaneous surge in inflation and policy tightening, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 5-year avg AND FEDFUNDS > 5-year avg in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 5-year averages in the same month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer balance sheets, which boosts demand for goods and services and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS above their 12-month averages in the same month signals a soft labor market with expanding employment, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 12-mo avg AND PAYEMS > 12-mo avg in same month
regime_hint: early recovery or soft labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both UNRATE and PAYEMS exceed their 12-month averages in the same month (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 2% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.05).
